descriptionChirho: The domain, rule, or sovereign authority of a king; encompasses both the abstract concept of royal power and the concrete territory over which a king reigns. Singular and plural forms represent the same lexical meaning with only grammatical number variation (160 singular + 3 plural occurrences). Multilingual evidence: spa 'reino/reinos,' hin 'राज्य/राज्यों,' arb 'مَلَكوتِ/مَمَالِكِ,' kor '나라/나라들,' swa 'ufalme/falme.' Overwhelmingly used in the phrase 'kingdom of God' or 'kingdom of heaven' in the Synoptics and John, but also of earthly kingdoms (Matt 4:8, 12:25-26; Luke 4:5; Rev 11:15, 16:10). The plural 'kingdoms' (Matt 4:8, Luke 4:5, Rev 11:15) refers to multiple earthly realms but shares the same core semantics.
